newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Doctors could set Yeltsin op. date "any day" - aide.
newsitem.headline: Doctors could set Yeltsin op. date "any day" - aide.

text.p: A date for Russian President Boris Yeltsin's heart operation could be set at any time, presidential spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky said on Friday.

Yastrzhembsky told a news conference he sympathised with a view expressed by top Russian surgeon Renat Akchurin that there was no need to announce the date in advance. "I find that point of view reasonable," he said.

But Yastrzhembsky made clear that reporters would still be told in advance about the date of the operation. He said Yeltsin's doctors were meeting every day and could decide at any one of these meetings when to operate.

Yeltsin said in early September that he had agreed to have an operation to improve the blood supply to his heart. He is currently in the Barvikha sanatorium outside Moscow while doctors carry out a final raft of tests.

U.S. specialist Michael DeBakey will advise Russian experts on the surgery, although Yastrzhembsky said foreign doctors would not be present in the operating theatre itself. He said DeBakey would arrive in Moscow on Saturday or Sunday.

Yastrzhembsky said Yeltsin had signed a decree giving Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin temporary authority to sign agreements with Russian regions. Chernomyrdin will take over all Yeltsin's powers, including control of the button which could be used to launch a nuclear strike, during the operation itself.
